chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamza, from Is'haq ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
He said to me: 'Cut your hair completely, so that its smell, its insects, and its dirt decrease, and your neck thickens, and your vision clears. And in another report: 'And your body rests.'
ai.seo_question: What are the physical and hygienic benefits of shaving or cutting hair according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the Prophetic tradition of *al-fafr* (shaving the head) as a means of hygiene and physical purification, linking bodily cleanliness to spiritual and physical well-being. The mention of thickening the neck and clarifying vision reflects the Shia scholarly understanding that external grooming practices have tangible physiological benefits, reinforcing the holistic nature of *Taharah* (purity) in Islamic jurisprudence. The additional note on bodily rest underscores the practical comfort derived from adhering to these Sunnah practices.
